newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end up on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end up on tight liquidity.

text.p: Pakistan's money market rates ended higher on Friday and are likely to remain up on Saturday on tight liquidity, dealers said.

"The market opened on a tight note and early overnight repos were traded at 19.75 percent," a dealer said. "Borrowers managed to bring the rates slightly down and some funds changed hands at 19 percent, but scarcity of funds pushed the rates back to 19.90 percent."
The dealers said most trades for the overnights were done between 19.50 and 20 percent and the day closed short once again.
Discounting for moderate amounts was reported at the State (central) Bank of Pakistan discount window, dealers said.
They said activity in term repos could not be witnessed as rates remaineed mismatched.
"One-month offers had no buyers at 17.50 percent and three-months bids and offers were quoted at 16 and 16.60 percent respectively.
